result.title: When Do Better Visual World Models Make Better Plans? Decision-Aligned Selection for Latent Planning
result.comment: Supplementary material will be included in the next version
result.summary: Visual world models enable goal-conditioned planning by predicting the outcomes of candidate actions in latent space. However, planning depends on how well a model ranks candidates, whereas training optimizes how accurately it predicts each one. We identify the Decision-Relevant Residual (DRR), the part of the cost error that can reorder candidates, and show that the more training reduces the DRR, the more it improves selection (Spearman $ρ= 0.82$, vs. $0.61$ for prediction error). Building on this insight, we introduce Decision-Aligned Selection (DAS), a plug-in selection rule that scores candidates by the standardized consensus of several independently trained checkpoints, which averages out their checkpoint-specific residuals. Across two model families (LeWorldModel and DINO-WM) and five tasks, DAS selects better actions than single checkpoints in 12 of 18 configurations and outperforms training one model three times longer in 14 of 18. In closed loop, DAS improves success over single checkpoints in 6 of 9 pre-registered LeWM comparisons.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究视觉世界模型的潜在规划表现取决于候选排序而非单步预测精度，提出 Decision-Relevant Residual 刻画会改变排序的代价误差，并给出即插即用的 Decision-Aligned Selection：用多个独立训练 checkpoint 的标准化共识为候选打分，在两个模型族、五个任务上验证其选动作与闭环成功率优势。
AI.relevance_reason: 「按排序/决策效果而非预测误差来评价与选择」的思路可能为 LVR 中多个 latent 假设的筛选、答案验证与 checkpoint 集成提供可核查线索；但原文面向视觉世界模型的机器人式规划，向语言推理状态迁移的有效性仍需核对。
